588	}
589	
590	/** Filter for the activity feed page and the audit-log CSV export. */
591	export interface ActivityFilter {
592	  readonly action?: readonly ActivityAction[];
593	  readonly actorId?: UserId;
594	  readonly projectId?: ProjectId;
595	  readonly subjectKind?: ActivitySubjectKind;
596	  readonly since?: IsoTimestamp;
597	  readonly until?: IsoTimestamp;
598	}
599	
600	/** Activity rows grouped by calendar day, as the feed renders them. */
601	export interface ActivityGroup {
602	  readonly day: string;
603	  readonly events: readonly ActivityEvent[];
604	}
605	import type {
606	  IsoTimestamp,
607	  MemberId,
608	  OrgId,
609	  SoftDeletable,
610	  TenantScoped,
611	  Timestamps,
612	  UserId,
613	  InvitationId,
614	} from "./common";
615	
616	/**
617	 * Taskflow RBAC roles, ordered from most to least privileged. `ROLE_RANK`
618	 * below is the single source of truth for "at least this role" comparisons —
619	 * never compare role strings directly.
620	 */
621	export type Role = "owner" | "admin" | "member" | "viewer";
622	
623	export const ROLES: readonly Role[] = ["owner", "admin", "member", "viewer"];
624	
625	export const ROLE_RANK: Readonly<Record<Role, number>> = {
626	  owner: 4,
627	  admin: 3,
628	  member: 2,
629	  viewer: 1,
630	};
631	
632	export type MemberStatus = "active" | "invited" | "suspended";
633	
634	export interface User extends Timestamps {
635	  readonly id: UserId;
636	  readonly email: string;
637	  readonly name: string;
638	  readonly avatarUrl: string | null;
639	  readonly timezone: string;
640	  readonly emailVerifiedAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
641	}
642	
643	export interface Member extends Timestamps, TenantScoped, SoftDeletable {
644	  readonly id: MemberId;
645	  readonly userId: UserId;
646	  readonly role: Role;
647	  readonly status: MemberStatus;
648	  readonly invitedBy: UserId | null;
649	  readonly joinedAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
650	  readonly lastSeenAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
651	}
652	
653	/** A member joined with the user record it points at, for list UIs. */
654	export interface MemberWithUser extends Member {
655	  readonly user: User;
656	}
657	
658	export interface Invitation extends Timestamps, TenantScoped {
659	  readonly id: InvitationId;
660	  readonly email: string;
661	  readonly role: Role;
662	  readonly invitedBy: UserId;
663	  readonly token: string;
664	  readonly expiresAt: IsoTimestamp;
665	  readonly acceptedAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
666	  readonly revokedAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
667	}
668	
669	/**
670	 * The authenticated principal for one request, always resolved for exactly one
671	 * organization. Everything that authorizes a mutation takes an `Actor` — see
672	 * `can()` in `src/lib/permissions.ts` and `assertOrgScope()` in
673	 * `src/lib/tenant.ts`.
674	 */
675	export interface Actor {
676	  readonly userId: UserId;
677	  readonly orgId: OrgId;
678	  readonly role: Role;
679	  /** Staff impersonation / internal tooling escape hatch. Defaults to false. */
680	  readonly isPlatformStaff?: boolean;
681	}
682	
683	export interface SessionPrincipal {
684	  readonly userId: UserId;
685	  readonly email: string;
686	  readonly activeOrgId: OrgId | null;
687	  readonly expiresAt: IsoTimestamp;
688	}
689	
690	/** True when `role` is at least as privileged as `atLeast`. */
691	export function hasRoleAtLeast(role: Role, atLeast: Role): boolean {
692	  return ROLE_RANK[role] >= ROLE_RANK[atLeast];
693	}
694	import type {
695	  CommentId,
696	  IssueId,
697	  MemberId,
698	  OrgId,
699	  ProjectId,
700	  UserId,
701	  WebhookId,
702	} from "./common";
703	import type { Role } from "./member";
704	import type { ProjectVisibility } from "./project";
705	
706	/**
707	 * The complete action vocabulary of `can()`. Every authorization decision in
708	 * Taskflow names one of these — there is no free-form string permission.
709	 */
710	export type PermissionAction =
711	  | "org:read"
712	  | "org:update"
713	  | "org:delete"
714	  | "org:manage_billing"
715	  | "org:manage_flags"
716	  | "member:read"
717	  | "member:invite"
718	  | "member:update_role"
719	  | "member:remove"
720	  | "project:create"
721	  | "project:read"
722	  | "project:update"
723	  | "project:archive"
724	  | "project:delete"
725	  | "issue:create"
726	  | "issue:read"
727	  | "issue:update"
728	  | "issue:assign"
729	  | "issue:archive"
730	  | "issue:delete"
731	  | "comment:create"
732	  | "comment:read"
733	  | "comment:update"
734	  | "comment:delete"
735	  | "activity:read"
736	  | "activity:export"
737	  | "notification:read"
738	  | "notification:manage"
739	  | "webhook:manage";
740	
741	/**
742	 * The object a permission is asked about. Discriminated on `kind` so the
743	 * ownership rules inside `can()` can read the fields they need without casts.
744	 */
745	export type PermissionResource =
746	  | { readonly kind: "organization"; readonly orgId: OrgId }
747	  | { readonly kind: "billing"; readonly orgId: OrgId }
748	  | {
749	      readonly kind: "member";
750	      readonly orgId: OrgId;
751	      readonly memberId: MemberId;
752	      readonly targetUserId: UserId;
753	      readonly targetRole: Role;
754	    }
755	  | {
756	      readonly kind: "project";
757	      readonly orgId: OrgId;
758	      readonly projectId: ProjectId;
759	      readonly visibility: ProjectVisibility;
760	      readonly leadId: UserId | null;
761	    }
762	  | {
763	      readonly kind: "issue";
764	      readonly orgId: OrgId;
765	      readonly projectId: ProjectId;
766	      readonly issueId: IssueId;
767	      readonly authorId: UserId;
768	      readonly assigneeId: UserId | null;
769	    }
770	  | {
771	      readonly kind: "comment";
772	      readonly orgId: OrgId;
773	      readonly commentId: CommentId;
774	      readonly authorId: UserId;
775	    }
776	  | { readonly kind: "activity"; readonly orgId: OrgId }
777	  | { readonly kind: "notification"; readonly orgId: OrgId; readonly recipientId: UserId }
778	  | { readonly kind: "webhook"; readonly orgId: OrgId; readonly webhookId: WebhookId | null };
779	
780	export type PermissionResourceKind = PermissionResource["kind"];
781	
782	/** Verbose form of a decision, used by the settings UI to explain a denial. */
783	export interface PermissionDecision {
784	  readonly allowed: boolean;
785	  readonly action: PermissionAction;
786	  readonly resourceKind: PermissionResourceKind;
787	  readonly reason:
788	    | "granted_by_role"
789	    | "granted_by_ownership"
790	    | "granted_by_staff"
791	    | "denied_by_role"
792	    | "denied_cross_tenant"
793	    | "denied_unknown_action";
794	}
795	import type {
796	  EventHandler,
797	  TaskflowEventMap,
798	  TaskflowEventPayload,
799	  TaskflowEventType,
800	  Unsubscribe,
801	} from "@/types/event";
802	
803	/**
804	 * In-process, typed publish/subscribe bus.
805	 *
806	 * Taskflow keeps `IssueService`, `NotificationService`, `ActivityService`, the
807	 * search indexer and the webhook dispatcher decoupled: writers `emit()`, and
808	 * every reactive concern `subscribe()`s at module init (see
809	 * `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`). Handlers are isolated — one
810	 * throwing handler never fails the emit or the sibling handlers.
811	 */
812	
813	type HandlerSet = Set<EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>>;
814	
815	const handlers = new Map<TaskflowEventType, HandlerSet>();
816	
817	const errorSinks = new Set<(type: TaskflowEventType, error: unknown) => void>();
818	
819	/** Registers a handler for one event type. Call the return value to detach. */
820	export function subscribe<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
821	  type: K,
822	  handler: EventHandler<K>,
823	): Unsubscribe {
824	  const set = handlers.get(type) ?? new Set();
825	  set.add(handler as EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>);
826	  handlers.set(type, set);
827	  return () => {
828	    set.delete(handler as EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>);
829	  };
830	}
831	
832	/** Registers a handler that detaches itself after the first delivery. */
833	export function subscribeOnce<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
834	  type: K,
835	  handler: EventHandler<K>,
836	): Unsubscribe {
837	  const off = subscribe(type, (payload) => {
838	    off();
839	    return handler(payload);
840	  });
841	  return off;
842	}
843	
844	/**
845	 * Publishes an event to every subscriber. Resolves once all handlers settle;
846	 * rejected handlers are reported to the error sinks, never rethrown.
847	 */
848	export async function emit<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
849	  type: K,
850	  payload: TaskflowEventPayload<K>,
851	): Promise<void> {
852	  const set = handlers.get(type);
853	  if (!set || set.size === 0) return;
854	
855	  const results = await Promise.allSettled(
856	    [...set].map(async (handler) => {
857	      await (handler as EventHandler<K>)(payload);
858	    }),
859	  );
860	
861	  for (const result of results) {
862	    if (result.status === "rejected") {
863	      reportHandlerError(type, result.reason);
864	    }
865	  }
866	}
867	
868	/** Fire-and-forget variant for call sites that must not await delivery. */
869	export function emitAndForget<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
870	  type: K,
871	  payload: TaskflowEventPayload<K>,
872	): void {
873	  void emit(type, payload).catch((error: unknown) => {
874	    reportHandlerError(type, error);
875	  });
876	}
877	
878	export function onHandlerError(
879	  sink: (type: TaskflowEventType, error: unknown) => void,
880	): Unsubscribe {
881	  errorSinks.add(sink);
882	  return () => {
883	    errorSinks.delete(sink);
884	  };
885	}
886	
887	function reportHandlerError(type: TaskflowEventType, error: unknown): void {
888	  for (const sink of errorSinks) {
889	    try {
890	      sink(type, error);
891	    } catch {
892	      // A failing error sink must never escalate.
893	    }
894	  }
895	}
896	
897	/** Number of live subscribers for an event; used by tests and diagnostics. */
898	export function subscriberCount(type: TaskflowEventType): number {
899	  return handlers.get(type)?.size ?? 0;
900	}
901	
902	/** Detaches every handler. Test-only — never call from application code. */
903	export function resetEventBus(): void {
904	  handlers.clear();
905	  errorSinks.clear();
906	}
907	
908	export type { TaskflowEventMap, TaskflowEventType, Unsubscribe };
909	/**
910	 * Cache tag vocabulary and revalidation helpers.
911	 *
912	 * Next 16 requires a cache-life profile as the second argument to
913	 * `revalidateTag`, which is exactly the kind of API change that rots when it
914	 * is spelled out at forty call sites. Server Actions call
915	 * `revalidateTagged([...])` and never import `next/cache` themselves.
916	 */
917	import { revalidateTag } from "next/cache";
918	import type { IssueId, OrgId, ProjectId } from "@/types/common";
919	
920	/** The cache-life profiles this app uses, by how stale a read may be. */
921	export const CACHE_PROFILES: Readonly<
922	  Record<"seconds" | "minutes" | "hours", string>
923	> = {
924	  seconds: "seconds",
925	  minutes: "minutes",
926	  hours: "hours",
927	};
928	
929	export function orgTag(orgId: OrgId): string {
930	  return `org:${orgId}`;
931	}
932	
933	export function projectTag(projectId: ProjectId): string {
934	  return `project:${projectId}`;
935	}
936	
937	export function issueTag(issueId: IssueId): string {
938	  return `issue:${issueId}`;
939	}
940	
941	/**
942	 * Invalidates every supplied tag under one profile, de-duplicating first so a
943	 * caller can splice together tag lists without worrying about repeats.
944	 */
945	export function revalidateTagged(
946	  tags: readonly string[],
947	  profile: string = CACHE_PROFILES.minutes,
948	): void {
949	  for (const tag of new Set(tags)) {
950	    if (tag === "") continue;
951	    revalidateTag(tag, profile);
952	  }
953	}

/**

/**
 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
 */
export async function runMigrations(
  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
): Promise<void> {
  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });

  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");

  try {
    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
      sqlite.exec(statement);
    }
  } finally {
    sqlite.close();
  }
}

/** `pnpm db:migrate` runs this file directly; importing it must stay inert. */
if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("migrate.ts") === true) {
  await runMigrations();
}

function readMigrationStatements(): readonly string[] {
  const dir = resolve(process.cwd(), MIGRATIONS_DIR);
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  const files = readdirSync(dir)
    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
    .sort();

  if (files.length === 0) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  return files.flatMap((name) =>
    readFileSync(join(dir, name), "utf8")
      .split("--> statement-breakpoint")
      .map((chunk) => chunk.trim())
      .filter(Boolean),

type HandlerSet = Set<EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>>;

const handlers = new Map<TaskflowEventType, HandlerSet>();

const errorSinks = new Set<(type: TaskflowEventType, error: unknown) => void>();

/** Registers a handler for one event type. Call the return value to detach. */
export function subscribe<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
  type: K,
  handler: EventHandler<K>,
): Unsubscribe {
  const set = handlers.get(type) ?? new Set();
  set.add(handler as EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>);
  handlers.set(type, set);
  return () => {
    set.delete(handler as EventHandler<TaskflowEventType>);
  };

/** Registers a handler that detaches itself after the first delivery. */
export function subscribeOnce<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
  type: K,
  handler: EventHandler<K>,
): Unsubscribe {
  const off = subscribe(type, (payload) => {
    off();
    return handler(payload);
  });
  return off;
}

/**
 * Publishes an event to every subscriber. Resolves once all handlers settle;
 * rejected handlers are reported to the error sinks, never rethrown.
 */
export async function emit<K extends TaskflowEventType>(
  type: K,
  payload: TaskflowEventPayload<K>,
): Promise<void> {
  const set = handlers.get(type);
  if (!set || set.size === 0) return;

  const results = await Promise.allSettled(
    [...set].map(async (handler) => {
      await (handler as EventHandler<K>)(payload);
    }),
  );

  for (const result of results) {

): void {

): Unsubscribe {
  errorSinks.add(sink);

  for (const sink of errorSinks) {

  seconds: "seconds",
  minutes: "minutes",
  hours: "hours",
};

export function orgTag(orgId: OrgId): string {
  return `org:${orgId}`;
}

export function projectTag(projectId: ProjectId): string {
  return `project:${projectId}`;
}

export function issueTag(issueId: IssueId): string {
  return `issue:${issueId}`;

 * caller can splice together tag lists without worrying about repeats.

export function revalidateTagged(
  tags: readonly string[],
  profile: string = CACHE_PROFILES.minutes,
): void {
  for (const tag of new Set(tags)) {
    if (tag === "") continue;
    revalidateTag(tag, profile);
  }
}

335	/**
336	 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
337	 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
338	 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
339	 */
340	export async function runMigrations(
341	  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
342	): Promise<void> {
343	  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
344	  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });
345	
346	  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
347	  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");
348	
349	  try {
350	    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
351	      sqlite.exec(statement);
352	    }
353	  } finally {
354	    sqlite.close();
355	  }
356	}
357	
358	/** `pnpm db:migrate` runs this file directly; importing it must stay inert. */
359	if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("migrate.ts") === true) {
360	  await runMigrations();
361	}
362	
363	function readMigrationStatements(): readonly string[] {
364	  const dir = resolve(process.cwd(), MIGRATIONS_DIR);
365	  if (!existsSync(dir)) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;
366	
367	  const files = readdirSync(dir)
368	    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
369	    .sort();
370	
371	  if (files.length === 0) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;
372	
373	  return files.flatMap((name) =>
374	    readFileSync(join(dir, name), "utf8")
375	      .split("--> statement-breakpoint")
376	      .map((chunk) => chunk.trim())
377	      .filter(Boolean),
378	  );
379	}
